Diff Lifecycle Events

The plugin fires User autocmds when a diff opens and closes, so you can react to the review lifecycle from your own config (resize windows, toggle a colorscheme, update a statusline, etc.). They are emitted regardless of auto_resize_terminal.

Event pattern When event.data fields
ClaudeCodeDiffOpened A proposed-edit diff has opened tab_name, file_path, new_file_path, is_new_file, diff_window, target_window, terminal_window, tab_number
ClaudeCodeDiffClosed The diff was accepted/rejected/closed tab_name, file_path, reason

reason is a best-effort, human-readable label (e.g. "diff accepted", "diff rejected", "replaced by new diff"); treat it as diagnostic text, not a stable enum to branch on. tab_number is only set when the diff opened in its own tab, and terminal_window may be nil if no Claude terminal is visible.

To fully own the terminal width during diffs, set diff_opts.auto_resize_terminal = false (so the plugin applies no width policy of its own) and resize from the events yourself. Note this is "own the width via the events", not "freeze the width": the diff layout still runs wincmd =, which equalizes splits, so set your desired width in the ClaudeCodeDiffOpened handler — it fires after the layout is built, so it wins. When the diff closes, the windows of the tab it split get back the sizes they had before it (if that tab still has the same window layout and the same space for it), and then ClaudeCodeDiffClosed fires:

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
  pattern = "ClaudeCodeDiffOpened",
  callback = function(ev)
    local term = ev.data.terminal_window
    if term and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(term) then
      vim.api.nvim_win_set_width(term, math.floor(vim.o.columns * 0.20))
    end
  end,
})

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
  pattern = "ClaudeCodeDiffClosed",
  callback = function(ev)
    -- restore your preferred idle layout here
  end,
})

For the common "just make the terminal narrower during diffs" case you don't need the events at all — set terminal.diff_split_width_percentage and leave auto_resize_terminal = true.

Working Directory Control

You can fix the Claude terminal's working directory regardless of autochdir and buffer-local cwd changes. Options (precedence order):

  • cwd_provider(ctx): function that returns a directory string. Receives { file, file_dir, cwd }.
  • cwd: static path to use as working directory.
  • git_repo_cwd = true: resolves git root from the current file directory (or cwd if no file).

A cwd_provider result or a cwd that starts with ~ or $ always goes through vim.fn.expand, so ~/projects/my-app and $HOME/my-app work. Any other text that names an existing folder is used as written, so a folder name with $, \, [ or { in it works. Other text goes through expand too.

Examples:

require("claudecode").setup({
  -- Top-level aliases are supported and forwarded to terminal config
  git_repo_cwd = true,
})

require("claudecode").setup({
  terminal = {
    cwd = vim.fn.expand("~/projects/my-app"),
  },
})

require("claudecode").setup({
  terminal = {
    cwd_provider = function(ctx)
      -- Prefer repo root; fallback to file's directory
      local cwd = require("claudecode.cwd").git_root(ctx.file_dir or ctx.cwd) or ctx.file_dir or ctx.cwd
      return cwd
    end,
  },
})

Terminal Buffer Filetype

The native and snacks providers set the filetype of the Claude terminal buffer to claudecode, so autocmds and ftplugins can target it. For example, to keep the Claude buffer out of the buffer list (#201):

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("FileType", {
  pattern = "claudecode",
  callback = function(args)
    vim.bo[args.buf].buflisted = false
  end,
})

  • native sets the filetype once per terminal, after the job starts, so buftype is already terminal in the handler.

  • snacks sets it through the Snacks window options (bo.filetype). That replaces the snacks_terminal filetype that snacks.nvim gives its terminals, so a FileType snacks_terminal autocmd no longer matches the Claude buffer. To get the Snacks filetype back, or to pick another name, set it in snacks_win_opts:

    terminal = {
  snacks_win_opts = { bo = { filetype = "snacks_terminal" } }, -- or any filetype you like
}

    Only snacks_win_opts changes it. A bo.filetype in your global snacks.nvim config (styles.terminal or terminal.win), or in a style that snacks_win_opts names, does not apply to the Claude buffer.

    Snacks applies bo when it creates the buffer, before the job starts (buftype is still nofile) and before it opens the window. So a window option set in the handler (vim.opt_local.colorcolumn = ...) does not reach the Claude window. Use snacks_win_opts.wo for that. Snacks applies bo again when it re-creates a floating window that was closed, so FileType can fire twice for one buffer. Keep the handler idempotent.

  • external and none create no Neovim buffer, so they set no filetype.

Suspending Neovim with Ctrl-Z

A Neovim terminal passes Ctrl-Z to its job, and Claude Code then suspends itself. Nothing in the terminal can resume it (#194). So the native and snacks providers map <C-z> in terminal mode on the Claude terminal buffer to :suspend. Ctrl-Z there suspends Neovim, as it does in any other window. The mapping is buffer-local, so other terminals keep their own Ctrl-Z behavior. external and none create no Neovim buffer, so they map nothing.

The buffer-local mapping shadows a global terminal-mode <C-z> mapping of yours in the Claude buffer. To keep your own mapping there, set it buffer-local for the Claude buffer. The plugin keeps a buffer-local <C-z> terminal mapping that already exists. For example, to send Ctrl-Z to Claude Code again:

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("FileType", {
  pattern = "claudecode", -- the filetype of the Claude buffer (see Terminal Buffer Filetype above)
  callback = function(args)
    vim.keymap.set("t", "<C-z>", "<C-z>", { buffer = args.buf })
  end,
})

  • Replace the mapping with vim.keymap.set, as the example does. Do not remove it with vim.keymap.del on snacks: Snacks fires FileType before the plugin maps <C-z>, so the handler finds nothing to delete, and the plugin then maps its default. On native, the plugin maps first, so vim.keymap.del works there.

  • The pattern must match the filetype of the Claude buffer. With snacks, if you changed it in snacks_win_opts.bo.filetype, use that filetype. To avoid the filetype, set the mapping from snacks_win_opts.on_buf, which the plugin calls before it maps <C-z>:

    terminal = {
  snacks_win_opts = {
    on_buf = function(win)
      vim.keymap.set("t", "<C-z>", "<C-z>", { buffer = win.buf })
    end,
  },
}

Leaving Terminal Mode in the Claude Terminal

With the native and snacks providers (external and none create no Neovim buffer), the Claude terminal runs in terminal mode. There Neovim sends your keys to Claude Code, so <C-w>h and your Normal-mode window mappings do nothing. A single <Esc> does not leave terminal mode either: it goes to Claude Code, which acts on it itself (#53, #77). With the snacks provider, a double-tap of <Esc> (two presses within about 200 ms) does leave terminal mode, but the first press still reaches Claude Code.

The plugin maps no key that leaves terminal mode or moves between windows, so you choose them:

  • <C-\><C-n> works with no setup. Neovim handles it, so Claude Code never sees it. You stay in the Claude window in Normal mode, and <C-w>h and the other window commands work. To type to Claude Code again, press i in the Claude window. When you come back to it from another window with the default terminal.auto_insert = true, :ClaudeCodeFocus enters terminal mode with either provider. <C-w>l and the other window commands do so only with snacks, or with native after a diff opened in a new tab (diff_opts.open_in_new_tab) has put the terminal in its tab, until that terminal window closes, even if it shows another buffer by then. With auto_insert = false, none of them do.
  • A shorter key is a mapping in a FileType autocmd for claudecode (see Terminal Buffer Filetype above). It exists on the Claude buffer only, so other terminals keep their keys, and a single <Esc> still goes to Claude Code.

To switch windows with <C-h>, <C-j>, <C-k> and <C-l> (each key leaves terminal mode and moves to the window in that direction, or stays in the Claude window when there is none):

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("FileType", {
  pattern = "claudecode",
  callback = function(args)
    for _, key in ipairs({ "h", "j", "k", "l" }) do
      vim.keymap.set("t", "<C-" .. key .. ">", "<C-\\><C-n><C-w>" .. key, {
        buffer = args.buf,
        desc = "Leave terminal mode and move to the window in direction " .. key,
      })
    end
  end,
})

To leave terminal mode and stay in the Claude window, here with <C-q>:

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("FileType", {
  pattern = "claudecode",
  callback = function(args)
    vim.keymap.set("t", "<C-q>", "<C-\\><C-n>", { buffer = args.buf, desc = "Leave terminal mode" })
  end,
})

A key you map no longer reaches Claude Code, so pick keys you do not need there. The first example takes <C-j> (new line), <C-k> (delete to the end of the line) and <C-l> (redraw the screen) away from the Claude Code prompt. Its interactive mode reference lists them and lists no binding for <C-h> or <C-q>. Do not map <Esc>: the snacks provider sets its own <Esc> key on the Claude buffer, and it replaces a mapping from your autocmd.

If <C-h> and the others clash with tmux or a navigation plugin, use <A-h> and the others instead (write "<A-" for "<C-" in the first block). On macOS, <A-h> fires only when your terminal sends Option as Meta, and many terminals need that turned on first (see Claude Code's Option key setup). These keys move between Neovim windows only. To move between tmux panes as well, use vim-tmux-navigator: map the key to <C-\><C-n><Cmd>TmuxNavigateLeft<CR> (and TmuxNavigateDown, TmuxNavigateUp, TmuxNavigateRight) in place of <C-\><C-n><C-w>h.

In a floating Claude window (snacks_win_opts.position = "float"), the four keys all go back to the window you came from.

When a diff opens in the tab where a floating Claude terminal sits, the plugin hides the float so it does not cover the diff, and the diff window has focus. A float that the user shows while the diff is open stays visible until another diff opens in that tab. The float stays hidden when the diff closes, and :ClaudeCodeFocus brings it back. A diff in its own tab leaves a visible float in the original tab alone while it is open. A diff is in its own tab with open_in_new_tab, and a split diff also opens in a new tab on its own when its tab already shows a diff. When a diff in its own tab closes, the plugin shows the terminal again if a window of it was visible in any tab when the diff opened, and none is visible then. A terminal split that another diff's new tab shows counts. The close does not look at other open diffs, so it can show the float over a diff that is still open: diff A hides the float, diff B opens in a new tab, diff C opens in another new tab while B's tab shows the terminal, and the close of C after the close of B shows the float over A. With diff_opts.keep_terminal_focus = true, the float stays on screen and keeps focus, and it covers the diff.

}

Notes:

  • No windows/buffers are created. :ClaudeCode and related commands will not open anything.
  • The WebSocket server still starts and broadcasts work as usual. Launch the Claude CLI externally when desired.
  • focus_after_send has no effect here (there is no in-editor terminal to focus); enabling it logs a one-time warning at startup. To focus your external session after a send, hook the User ClaudeCodeSendComplete event.

Custom Terminal Providers

You can create custom terminal providers by passing a table with the required functions instead of a string provider name:

require("claudecode").setup({
  terminal = {
    provider = {
      -- Required functions
      setup = function(config)
        -- Initialize your terminal provider
      end,

      open = function(cmd_string, env_table, effective_config, focus)
        -- Open terminal with command and environment
        -- focus parameter controls whether to focus terminal (defaults to true)
      end,

      close = function()
        -- Close the terminal
      end,

      simple_toggle = function(cmd_string, env_table, effective_config)
        -- Simple show/hide toggle
      end,

      focus_toggle = function(cmd_string, env_table, effective_config)
        -- Smart toggle: focus terminal if not focused, hide if focused
      end,

      get_active_bufnr = function()
        -- Return terminal buffer number or nil
        return 123 -- example
      end,

      is_available = function()
        -- Return true if provider can be used
        return true
      end,

      -- Optional functions (auto-generated if not provided)
      toggle = function(cmd_string, env_table, effective_config)
        -- Defaults to calling simple_toggle for backward compatibility
      end,

      _get_terminal_for_test = function()
        -- For testing only, defaults to return nil
        return nil
      end,
    },
  },
})

Custom Provider Example

Here's a complete example using a hypothetical my_terminal plugin:

local my_terminal_provider = {
  setup = function(config)
    -- Store config for later use
    self.config = config
  end,

  open = function(cmd_string, env_table, effective_config, focus)
    if focus == nil then focus = true end

    local my_terminal = require("my_terminal")
    my_terminal.open({
      cmd = cmd_string,
      env = env_table,
      width = effective_config.split_width_percentage,
      side = effective_config.split_side,
      focus = focus,
    })
  end,

  close = function()
    require("my_terminal").close()
  end,

  simple_toggle = function(cmd_string, env_table, effective_config)
    require("my_terminal").toggle()
  end,

  focus_toggle = function(cmd_string, env_table, effective_config)
    local my_terminal = require("my_terminal")
    if my_terminal.is_focused() then
      my_terminal.hide()
    else
      my_terminal.focus()
    end
  end,

  get_active_bufnr = function()
    return require("my_terminal").get_bufnr()
  end,

  is_available = function()
    local ok, _ = pcall(require, "my_terminal")
    return ok
  end,
}

require("claudecode").setup({
  terminal = {
    provider = my_terminal_provider,
  },
})

The custom provider will automatically fall back to the native provider if validation fails or is_available() returns false.

Optional functions: ensure_visible() shows the terminal without focusing it. hide_float(tab) hides the terminal when it is a visible floating window, and when tab is not nil only when that window is in tab. It returns true when it did. The plugin calls it with the diff's tab when a diff opens in the tab of a floating terminal, so the float does not cover the diff, unless diff_opts.keep_terminal_focus is set. A provider that ignores tab hides its float in any tab. A diff does not show the float again, except that a diff in its own tab calls ensure_visible() in the original tab when it closes (in the current tab when the original tab is gone), if a window of the terminal was visible in any tab when the diff opened. :ClaudeCodeSend, :ClaudeCodeAdd and :ClaudeCodeTreeAdd also call ensure_visible() after a send to a connected Claude (they call open instead with focus_after_send, or when Claude is not connected).

Note: If your command or working directory may contain spaces or special characters, prefer returning a table of args from a function (e.g., { "alacritty", "--working-directory", cwd, "-e", "claude", "--help" }) to avoid shell-quoting issues.

Auto-Save Plugin Issues

Using auto-save plugins can cause diff windows opened by Claude to immediately accept without waiting for input. You can avoid this using a custom condition:

Pocco81/auto-save.nvim 
opts = {
  -- ... other options
  condition = function(buf)
    local fn = vim.fn
    local utils = require("auto-save.utils.data")

    -- First check the default conditions
    if not (fn.getbufvar(buf, "&modifiable") == 1 and utils.not_in(fn.getbufvar(buf, "&filetype"), {})) then
      return false
    end

    -- Exclude claudecode diff buffers by buffer name patterns
    local bufname = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(buf)
    if bufname:match("%(proposed%)") or
       bufname:match("%(NEW FILE %- proposed%)") or
       bufname:match("%(New%)") then
      return false
    end

    -- Exclude by buffer variables (claudecode sets these)
    if vim.b[buf].claudecode_diff_tab_name or
       vim.b[buf].claudecode_diff_new_win or
       vim.b[buf].claudecode_diff_target_win then
      return false
    end

    -- Exclude by buffer type (claudecode diff buffers use "acwrite")
    local buftype = fn.getbufvar(buf, "&buftype")
    if buftype == "acwrite" then
      return false
    end

    return true -- Safe to auto-save
  end,
},

Troubleshooting

  • First stop: Run :checkhealth claudecode — it verifies the Claude CLI is installed, the WebSocket server is running, the lock file exists and can be read, and whether Claude is connected
  • Claude not connecting? Check :ClaudeCodeStatus and verify lock file exists in ~/.claude/ide/ (or $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/ide/ if CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set and not empty)
  • Need debug logs? Set log_level = "debug" in opts
  • Terminal issues? Try provider = "native" if using snacks.nvim
  • Local installation not working? If you used claude migrate-installer, set terminal_cmd = "~/.claude/local/claude" in your config. Check which claude vs ls ~/.claude/local/claude to verify your installation type.
  • Native binary installation not working? If you used the alpha native binary installer, run claude doctor to verify installation health and use which claude to find the binary path. Set terminal_cmd = "/path/to/claude" with the detected path in your config.

Repository Blueprint

This section is the contract map of the source tree. Each linked README lists the interface, invariants, and side effects of one package.

System Overview

Neovim loads plugin/claudecode.lua, which guards the load and can schedule require("claudecode").setup(). setup in lua/claudecode validates config, sets up the logger, terminal, and diff modules, calls start when auto_start is true, and then registers the :ClaudeCode* commands. start opens the WebSocket server on 127.0.0.1, writes a lock file with an auth token, and enables selection tracking when track_selection is true. The Claude CLI finds the lock file, connects, and calls the MCP tools. The plugin runs the CLI through a terminal provider. Files under scripts/ are dev and release tooling and are never loaded by the plugin.

Local Interface & Invariants

  • dev-config.lua returns a lazy.nvim plugin spec for local development: "coder/claudecode.nvim" with dev = true, a cmd list of :ClaudeCode* command stubs (it omits ClaudeCodeSendText), <leader>a* keys mappings, and opts that set only focus_after_send = true [dev-config.lua:return]. The plugin never requires it. It has no side effects until a user symlinks it into a Neovim config (see the comment at the top of the file).

Subdirectories & System Boundaries

  • lua: ./lua/README.md - Neovim Lua runtime path. It holds only the claudecode package.
  • lua/claudecode: ./lua/claudecode/README.md - Core package: setup, commands, config, lock file, terminal dispatcher, blocking diffs, selection tracking, explorer integrations, logging, and :checkhealth.
  • lua/claudecode/server: ./lua/claudecode/server/README.md - Pure-Lua RFC 6455 WebSocket and JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP server on vim.loop TCP, with auth-token-checked upgrade and a keep-alive ping timer.
  • lua/claudecode/terminal: ./lua/claudecode/terminal/README.md - Terminal providers (native, snacks, external, none) and paste_fix for Neovim < 0.12.2.
  • lua/claudecode/tools: ./lua/claudecode/tools/README.md - MCP tool registry: 10 tools in tools/list plus the hidden close_tab. openDiff runs in a coroutine and defers its response.
  • plugin: ./plugin/README.md - Runtime loader: Neovim >= 0.8.0 check, vim.g.loaded_claudecode guard, and optional vim.g.claudecode_auto_setup.
  • scripts: ./scripts/README.md - Issue repro scripts, the integration test runner, a manual openDiff helper, and the release-please runner.

fixtures/ (Neovim configs for manual repros) holds repro notes (README.md in some folders) but no EGM contracts. tests/ (Busted specs) holds no contracts.

Global Invariants

  • The server listens only on 127.0.0.1 [lua/claudecode/server/tcp.lua:M._bind_and_listen].
  • A WebSocket upgrade must carry x-claude-code-ide-authorization that matches the lock-file token, compared in constant time [lua/claudecode/server/handshake.lua:M.validate_upgrade_request]. start returns false before it starts the server if the token is shorter than 10 characters. If the token does not match the token that lockfile.create wrote, it tries to remove the lock file (a failed removal is only logged) and stops the server [lua/claudecode/init.lua:M.start].
  • The token comes from vim.loop.random or /dev/urandom, never math.random [lua/claudecode/lockfile.lua:get_random_bytes].
  • Lock files live in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/ide, or in ~/.claude/ide when that variable is unset or empty, named <port>.lock [lua/claudecode/lockfile.lua:M.lock_dir]. repro_issue_238.sh, repro_issue_248.sh, and the verify skill's ws-client.mjs read the port from that basename [scripts/repro_issue_238.sh:PORT] [scripts/repro_issue_248.sh:PORT] [.agents/skills/verify-claudecode-nvim/scripts/ws-client.mjs:port]. repro_issue_70.sh and repro_issue_277.sh get the port another way.
  • :ClaudeCode* commands exist only after setup runs [lua/claudecode/init.lua:M._create_commands]. The loader defines none [plugin/claudecode.lua].
  • openDiff must run in a non-main coroutine. Its response is deferred until the diff resolves [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:M.open_diff_blocking] [lua/claudecode/server/init.lua:M._setup_deferred_response]. The user resolves it by accepting or rejecting it. The plugin also rejects a pending diff when the server stops [lua/claudecode/server/init.lua:M.stop], when the client that opened it disconnects [lua/claudecode/server/init.lua:M.start], or when a new diff reuses its tab_name [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:M.open_diff_blocking]. Claude's close_tab and closeAllDiffTabs calls also reject a pending diff [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:M.close_diff_by_tab_name]. A diff that resolves before openDiff yields, for example from a ClaudeCodeDiffOpened handler, is answered at once [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:M.open_diff_blocking].
  • Exit answers. This bullet is the one place that states what Claude gets when Neovim exits. The other docs describe how the code runs the exit and point here. A call is waiting when its openDiff setup has finished and nobody has answered its diff. Each fact below was probed with a real WebSocket client on Neovim 0.8.0, 0.9.5, 0.10.4, 0.11.5 and 0.12.3. SIGKILL stands in for a crash, which was not probed:
    • An exit that runs VimLeavePre (:qa!, SIGTERM or SIGHUP) gives each waiting call one DIFF_REJECTED [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:cleanup_at_exit]. A call that already has its answer, such as a FILE_SAVED, gets no second one.
    • A call that the exit cuts off during its openDiff setup gets one -32603 error from the server stop. It has no response sender yet, so nothing else can answer it. This happens when a nested = true ClaudeCodeDiffOpened handler runs :qa! during the setup. A server stop that is not an exit, for example :ClaudeCodeStop from such a handler, gives the same error [lua/claudecode/server/init.lua:M.stop] [lua/claudecode/server/init.lua:M._handle_request].
    • The answers go out before the server closes each client with close code 1001. stop also tries to remove the lock file [lua/claudecode/init.lua:M.stop].
    • SIGKILL, a crash, :noautocmd qa!, a Lua os.exit() and a :qa! from inside an autocmd that is not nested run no VimLeavePre. A :qa!, SIGTERM or SIGHUP that Neovim handles while an autocmd that is not nested is still running can end Neovim without VimLeavePre too. A synchronous LSP format on save, which waits in vim.wait, is the common example. In these exits, Claude gets no answer, its socket closes with 1006, and the lock file stays.
    • In an exit that runs VimLeavePre, the autocmd of ClaudeCodeMCPDiff rejects every diff with the status pending first and removes every diff after that [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:cleanup_at_exit]. A reject can remove its own diff at once. With the default on_new_file_reject = "keep_empty", a new-file diff in the vertical or horizontal layout that is not in its own tab is removed when it is rejected, so its ClaudeCodeDiffClosed handler runs while a later diff is still pending [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:M._resolve_diff_as_rejected]. With "close_window", both waiting calls have their answers before the first ClaudeCodeDiffClosed fires (probed in the vertical, horizontal and unified layouts with one new-file and one existing-file diff, for :qa! and SIGTERM). A call that the exit cuts off during its setup is not waiting: it gets its -32603 after the ClaudeCodeDiffClosed events, in every layout and with either on_new_file_reject (probed with a nested :qa! in a ClaudeCodeDiffOpened handler, on each Neovim version above). Every call still gets one answer before the server closes its client with 1001.
    • How the code runs the exit: lua/claudecode/README.md and the Resource Cleanup section of ARCHITECTURE.md.

Global Side Effects

  • Lock file: start writes <port>.lock (file 0600, atomic rename). A new lock directory gets 0700, and the chmod of an existing one is best-effort [lua/claudecode/lockfile.lua:M.create]. stop tries to delete it and logs a warning when it cannot [lua/claudecode/lockfile.lua:M.remove] [lua/claudecode/init.lua:M.stop]. The ClaudeCodeShutdown VimLeavePre autocmd runs stop [lua/claudecode/init.lua:M.setup].
  • Network: one loopback TCP listener [lua/claudecode/server/init.lua:M.start] plus WebSocket frames and JSON-RPC broadcasts [lua/claudecode/server/init.lua:M.broadcast]: selection_changed [lua/claudecode/selection.lua:M.send_selection_update] and at_mentioned [lua/claudecode/init.lua:M._broadcast_at_mention].
  • Processes: the terminal provider spawns the Claude CLI with ENABLE_IDE_INTEGRATION, FORCE_CODE_TERMINAL, loopback no_proxy/NO_PROXY, and, while the server runs, CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT [lua/claudecode/terminal.lua:get_claude_command_and_env]. :checkhealth claudecode runs the CLI with --version [lua/claudecode/health.lua:check_cli]. With terminal.git_repo_cwd, the terminal module runs git rev-parse --show-toplevel [lua/claudecode/cwd.lua:M.git_root].
  • Disk: open_diff writes diff temp files under stdpath("cache")/claudecode_diffs, or stdpath("cache")/claudecode_diffs_fallback when a directory cannot be created in the first. If both fail, it returns an error that names both directories [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:create_temp_file]. The openDiff tool writes no temp files [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:M.open_diff_blocking]. The saveDocument tool writes an open buffer to its file [lua/claudecode/tools/save_document.lua:handler].
  • Editor state: autocmd groups (ClaudeCodeShutdown, ClaudeCodeSelection, ClaudeCodeMCPDiff, ClaudeCodeDiffCleanup, ClaudeCodeNativeAdopted, ClaudeCodeOpenFileNewFiles, and snacks_win_<id>, one per Snacks terminal whose split the plugin re-creates [lua/claudecode/terminal/snacks.lua:register_window_events]), nvim_buf_attach change listeners on the buffer of a held selection and on every buffer where a visual selection starts, until the first edit after the selection ends [lua/claudecode/selection.lua:watch_selection_buffer], a vim.on_key listener (one namespace) that an edit of the buffer in which you select sets, at the latest until the next key [lua/claudecode/selection.lua:note_visual_edit], User events (ClaudeCodeSendComplete, ClaudeCodeDiffOpened, ClaudeCodeDiffClosed), the four global ClaudeCodeInlineDiff* highlight groups for the "unified" diff layout [lua/claudecode/diff_inline.lua:setup_highlights], and a wrapped global vim.paste when terminal.fix_streamed_paste is true, or "auto" on Neovim < 0.12.2 or a 0.12.2 prerelease [lua/claudecode/terminal/paste_fix.lua:M.apply] [lua/claudecode/terminal/paste_fix.lua:M.install] [lua/claudecode/terminal/paste_fix.lua:M.is_affected_version].
  • Lua globals: the server stores deferred openDiff response senders in _G.claude_deferred_responses [lua/claudecode/server/init.lua:M._setup_deferred_response]. The diff module calls and clears them [lua/claudecode/diff.lua:M.open_diff_blocking]. _G.claudecode_clients_created counts connections [lua/claudecode/server/client.lua:M.create_client]. See the server README.
  • Release tooling: scripts/release-please-runner.js without --dry-run creates GitHub tags, releases, and PRs [scripts/release-please-runner.js:main].
